text:
sam: quick heads-up — ran a perf profile on the nightly kv/continuous-batching run and hit a cluster of OOM-like evictions when compact batches coalesced with long-prefix requests. attaching the short log snippet below and a sketch of a possible limiter. anyone seen this pattern before?

liz: ugh, saw something similar a while back but that was with the eager-prefetch patch. can you paste the exact trace?

sam: paste from node-3 logs: 
```
[2026-03-17T03:12:04Z] batch_coordinator: forming compact batch id=14532 tokens=3200 kv_reserve=45MB available_kv=60MB
[2026-03-17T03:12:04Z] kernel_switch: selected=opt64 seq_len=1024 estimated_kv=40MB
[2026-03-17T03:12:04Z] eviction: triggered soft-evict, freed=0MB
[2026-03-17T03:12:04Z] oom_guard: oom near miss, inflight_batches=3, total_kv_needed=140MB
[2026-03-17T03:12:04Z] batch_abandon: id=14532 reason=kv-pressure
```

sam: note the coordinator allowed a compact batch to allocate per-batch kv_reserve=45MB while two other in-flight long-prefixs already consumed most of the cache. we should avoid handing out that much budget purely based on per-request token estimates.

tyler: looks like the core issue is that compact-batch formation currently uses a static per-request kv-budget times num-requests heuristic. when long prefixes show up, those budgets sum badly. propose a sliding shared pool + per-batch cap:
```
compact_pool_max = max( min(global_kv_free * 0.6, 200MB), 32MB )
per_batch_cap = min(request_estimate_kv * 1.2, 64MB)
allocate = min(per_batch_cap, compact_pool_remaining)
```

liz: i like the shared pool idea. also we should bake in a short TTL for allocations so we can reclaim quickly if the batch stalls. e.g., allocation_ttl=200ms and a fast-retry path that reduces per-request kv_estimate by x%.

natalie: from infra side: if we reclaim too aggressively we might thrash the kernel selection (switching kernels repeatedly). keep in mind kernel_switch cost is ~1.8ms on p4d. reclaiming/reshaping batches should avoid causing extra kernel churn.

sam: good call. maybe combine both: short TTL but a grace_window that prevents kernel re-eval unless allocation changed > 20%.

tyler: quick experiment plan: 1) implement compact_pool_max = global_kv_free * 0.5, 2) per_batch_cap = clamp(estimated_kv*1.1, 16MB, 64MB), 3) allocation_ttl=150ms, 4) graceful_kernel_retain_pct=0.2. observe eviction events and kernel_switch_count.

opsbot: created perf-run:2026-03-17-compact-pool-experiment (jobs enqueued).

liz: also add a metric: "batch.kv_allocation_reason" (est|pool|fallback) so we can see when fallback-to-zero happens. and maybe record request token histogram per batch to refine per_batch_cap.

sam: agreed. one more data point from the run — memory sampling showed two long-prefix requests holding 70MB each while short inference batches expected 8–12MB. aggregate was the killer.

natalie: if we roll this to canary, i'd gate it behind a small target traffic % and enable an automatic revert if eviction_rate > 0.1% or kernel_switch_rate increases >15%.

sam: ok i'm on the impl. volunteers for review? @liz and @tyler can you eyeball the config patch and the metric names? i'll push a draft tomorrow morning and attach the perf run id. thanks :thumbsup:

liz: happy to review.

tyler: yep, I'll take the metric instrumentation.

natalie: I'll scope the canary conditions and monitoring alerts.

opsbot: perf-run:2026-03-17-compact-pool-experiment status=running queued=4"
